source: The rain hadn't let up in three days. Neither had my headache.

context.speaker: Sam Vale
context.note: Narration. A private detective's office at night.

source: Then she walked in, and the headache got worse.
Are you Sam Vale, the private investigator?
Depends who's asking, and how much they're paying.
My name is Lorraine Pike. My brother Eddie is missing.
People go missing every day in this city. Most of them want to.
Not Eddie. He'd never leave without telling me.
When did you see him last?
Last Tuesday. He said he had a job down at the docks.
What kind of job?
He wouldn't say. Only that it would pay off all his debts.
Jobs like that usually pay off in other ways.
Please, Mr. Vale. The police won't even look for him.
Fifty a day, plus expenses.
Here's two hundred. Find him.
Who did your brother owe money to?
He mentioned a bar. The Blue Lantern, on Fifth Street.
I know the place. The beer is warm and the customers are cold.
Will you call me as soon as you hear anything?
She left a trace of perfume and a lot of questions.
The Blue Lantern smelled like spilled whiskey and bad decisions.
Well, look who it is. Haven't seen you in a while, Vale.
I've been busy staying sober, Gus.
How's that going?
About as well as your business. Pour me a coffee.
Coffee? In my bar? You must be working.
I'm looking for a guy named Eddie Pike.
Never heard of him.
You answered that too fast, Gus.
Look, I don't want any trouble.
Nobody wants trouble. It shows up anyway.
Fine. He came in last week with Moretti's boys.
Moretti? The guy who runs the card games on the waterfront?
Keep your voice down, will you?
What did they talk about?
A shipment. Something coming in at Pier 9 on Friday night.
What kind of shipment?
The kind you don't ask about if you want to keep your teeth.
Thanks for the coffee, Gus. Put it on my tab.
You don't have a tab. You have a debt.
The precinct was as cheerful as a funeral, and twice as crowded.
Vale. Who let you in here?
Good to see you too, Lieutenant.
I've got five minutes. Make them count.
Eddie Pike. Missing since Tuesday. Anything come across your desk?
A lot of things come across my desk. Most of them I throw away.
His sister says he was mixed up with Moretti.
Then his sister should start picking out flowers.
You know something, Reyes.
I know that Moretti has friends in City Hall. Powerful friends.
And you're afraid of them.
I'm afraid of losing my pension. There's a difference.
Something's coming in at Pier 9 on Friday.
Where did you hear that?
A bartender with a bad memory and a good conscience.
Stay away from the docks, Vale. That's not a request.
Since when do you care what happens to me?
I don't. I just hate paperwork, and you'd make a lot of it.
I'll try to die somewhere outside your district.
He didn't laugh. Cops never do when the joke is too close to the truth.
Pier 9 at midnight. Fog so thick you could lean on it.
Hey! Who's out there?
Just a guy looking for his lost cat.
At this hour? Get lost before I call Mr. Moretti.
Go ahead. I've been wanting to meet him.
You've got a big mouth for a man standing alone in the dark.
I'm not alone. I brought my good looks.
Search him.
He's clean, boss. Just a wallet and a cheap lighter.
Where's Eddie Pike, Moretti?
Eddie? Eddie owes me money. Men who owe me money don't disappear.
Then where is he?
That's what I'd like to know. He ran off with my shipment.
So we're both looking for him.
The difference is, I'll find him first.
Funny. His sister didn't hire you.
His sister? Eddie doesn't have a sister.
That's when I realized I'd been played from the start.
Let him go. He's going to lead us right to her.
The fog swallowed me whole, and for once I was grateful.
